title: Pizzicato technique: symphony versus jazz bassists
summary: Mazzari explains good hand and thumb position, how to tell trained from untrained bassists, and praises Bob Ciccarelli, who plays everything in position.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, no, not blood. Blood from whales? It's got... I don't know. It's a squawk one. So, uh, I want to talk to you about playing the string bass. Oh, yeah, man. Okay. Ask me. How do you play the string bass pizzicato properly as compared with the way the jazz musicians play?
Well, uh, any good, uh, symphony bass player will play pizzicato properly and it's very easy to see why the, why the bass player is holding, is doing it. I mean, uh...
How does he hold his hand, for example? What about the fingerboard? Does he do anything with that?

Well, uh, you're getting... Okay. Too many questions at once. Too many questions at once. Okay. I'll tell you, uh... Don't get excited. Of course, uh... Am I interrupting you? More and more, you see now, good bass players playing jazz. Mm-hmm. Uh, you can, you can tell right away, you walk into a place and there's a band and you see a bass player. He's got his fingers on his strings, nice and straight, you know, and his elbow sticks out.
And level with his arm, you know, and you can tell that he's had a good schooling and, and...
Well, now where should the thumb be placed?
Well, right behind, between the second and third finger.
Behind the neck and between the second and third fingers. Yeah. It's all in the middle there.

Yeah, and a lot of guys, they just let the thumb stick up, you know, and they, and they just move their fingers up and down. Well, that's a hard way to do it. I mean, they're just making it harder on themselves. But of course, those are the guys who didn't study. They just picked up a bass and they call themselves bass players. Mm-hmm. Of course, they, they may know, some of them know the chords, but most of them don't. Actually, if, if it's, the guy is a good enough, intelligent enough fella who has the, you know, the... Well, that he goes out and tries to make things easier for him, he's better off. Mm-hmm. But you can tell the difference right away, a bass player. We're just looking at him, you can tell whether he's... been raised to play the bass correctly or whether he just picked it up. Of course, more good bass players now are getting into the jazz group now, you know. I can tell you a very successful one in town is Bob Ciccarelli.
Yeah, I was thinking about him.

Oh man, he does a terrific job. Well, there you are, you see, he had the advantage of having started playing symphony bass. He studied it properly. Now he can walk into any band and play anything or... because he plays everything in position. Can play all those runs and to him, they come easy. Uh, a lot of those cats I was telling you about, you just, you just can't do it.
They're out of tune then, if they don't play them in position, is that what that... Out of tune, they jump all over the board, up and down, you know.
How many strings do they play on those guys who don't know much?
Boy, I don't know. There's four strings. I doubt if they use them all. In other words, you see some real bad bass players sometimes. It just makes you...
